newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah firms in quiet late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah firms in quiet late trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah firmed against the dollar in quiet trading on Wednesday as major operators stayed on the sidelines, dealers said.
They said operators were generally absent from the Jakarta market and possibly from the region.
One Japanese bank dealer said there was no clear direction in the market and people just kept a wait-and-see attitude.
"We might have a better view on Thursday because operators can decide on new commitments as spot rate will due next week on September 3," the dealer said.
New York is closed for a public holiday on Monday.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,341.5/42.0 at 0915 GMT against an opening of 2,342.0/42.5.
Dealers said swap rates were stable as well in dull trade.
One U.S. bank dealer said earlier there were some small forward selling in the morning because of stable rate in the past few days and higher roll-over cost over the weekend.
However, dealers were cautious to sell aggressively because forward rates might have bottomed out at present.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,341.4/41.6 and 2,341.25/41.5, respectively.
Overnight swap was at 0.35/0.45 and tom/next at 0.45/0.52.
One-month swap was at 16.75/17.50, two at 34.0/35.5, three at 51.75/52.25 and six at 104.0/104.25 points.
The central bank raised its intervention rate by one point to 2,339/2,457 and the conversion rate also by one point to 2,339/2,385 on Wednesday.
